question: How do sample size and population shape change one-sample t inference?

randomness.effect_encoding: IEEE754 float64 little-endian uint64; -0.0 canonicalized to +0.0; low32=bits&0xffffffff; high32=bits>>32
randomness.consumption: one generator per cell; sequential row-major generation across batches; alpha and B are not in the RNG key
randomness.independence: independent pseudo-random draws within and between sample groups; fixed seed IDs provide reproducibility, not a proof of independence

inference.coverage: closed interval contains true mean mu0+sigma*d
inference.boundary: CI/test equivalence checks exclude isclose(abs(t), critical, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12); reported p and intervals are never adjusted
inference.invalid: retain B denominator and valid-only counts; any invalid group marks cell for investigation and aggregate rates/widths/intervals as NaN
inference.rate_intervals: 95% Wilson, descriptive per cell; not simultaneous acceptance bands
inference.width_sd: sample SD ddof=1 across B widths

normal_investigation_band.p: coverage=0.95; rejection=normal noncentral-t power (including alpha under d=0)
normal_investigation_band.interpretation: conservative investigation flag, not a proof/disproof and never a reason to redraw

H1.claim: Normal iid t intervals cover at nominal level; under H0 rejection matches alpha
H1.criterion: supported if all 27 normal coverage counts and all 9 normal d=0 rejection counts lie in preregistered conservative bands, with zero invalids; otherwise unresolved/investigate, retaining every result

H2.claim: For normal populations, increasing n narrows mean CI width and increases theoretical power at nonzero fixed d
H2.criterion: supported if mean widths strictly decrease for n=5,20,100 within each normal d/seed, normal theory power strictly increases at d=0.2,0.5, every normal empirical rejection count is in its conservative theory band, and no invalids; otherwise unresolved/investigate; no single-sample monotonicity claim

H3.claim: Matched mean/variance need not give nominal small-sample inference under a right-skewed population
H3.scope: n=5,d=0; larger n and nonzero effects reported descriptively, without a required recovery direction
H3.criterion: supported if coverage or rejection for centered_exponential lies outside its nominal conservative binomial count range in all three seeds, with the same direction across seeds, while all matched normal counts lie inside their nominal ranges and all six cells have zero invalids; otherwise unresolved/not supported by this fixed design
H3.nominal_band: same conservative count construction p=0.95 or0.05, tail=0.001/(2*54); descriptive comparator only, excluded from the 54 normal-theory checks
H3.direction: neither direction nor n=100 recovery is fixed as a desired conclusion

execution.first_fixed_run: once only; no automatic repeats, seed additions or outcome-dependent filtering
execution.bug_correction: at most one separately authorized rerun; retain old results, source version and reason; this runner refuses any existing attempt in a destination
execution.samples: raw observations are never saved; at most one batch plus B inference outputs per cell retained
execution.budget_response: stop, preserve completed rows and record incomplete cells/resources; do not expand limits
